sh.title: Shield
sh.hero.0.sub: No firewall, no ad blocking. Flip one on and your server stops being an open house.
sh.hero.1.sub: One shield's up. Turn on the other one for the full glow-up.
sh.hero.2.sub: Firewall's up and ads are getting ghosted. Your network's eating good.
sh.fw.onHint: Only what you allow gets in. Everything else? Left on read.
sh.fw.offHint: Every port that's listening can be reached rn.
sh.fw.onMsg: You stay connected: {client} keeps getting through on ports {ports}. You get a minute to hit Keep, or it undoes itself.
sh.fw.offMsg: Every listening port becomes reachable from your network again.
sh.fw.unsupported: The firewall needs NoCapOS running on Linux as root.
sh.fw.notInstalled: ufw isn't installed yet. It's the engine, Shield is the dashboard.
sh.fw.installYourself: The firewall can't be set up on this system.
sh.keep.title: Keep these changes?
sh.keep.body: Still here? Hit Keep. Undoing itself in {n}s.
sh.ov.liveHint: Each bar is a minute. Red is what got blocked.
sh.ov.allowWarn: Heads up: new connections are let in by default. Set incoming to Ghost and allow only what you need.
sh.exp.title: What's exposed
sh.exp.hint: Everything listening for other devices, and whether the firewall lets it through.
sh.exp.hintOff: The firewall's off, so all of these are open. Switches take effect once it's on.
sh.exp.none: Nothing's listening for other devices. Clean.
sh.exp.bypass: the container engine opens this itself
sh.preset.title: One-tap presets
sh.preset.hint: Allow common stuff in one tap.
sh.rule.title: Rules
sh.rule.hint: Checked top to bottom. First match wins.
sh.rule.none: No rules yet. The defaults run the show.
sh.rule.limitHint: Limit lets it in but slows down anyone who tries 6+ times in 30 seconds. Great for SSH.
sh.dns.offHint: Off by default. Turn it on and point your devices here to ghost ads and trackers.
sh.dns.onMsg: NoCapOS starts answering DNS on port 53 and downloads your block lists. Nothing changes for devices until you point them here.
sh.dns.useHereHint: This server's own lookups go through the blocker as well.
sh.dns.useTitle: Use the blocker on this server?
sh.dns.useMsg: This server will ask itself for every name. If the blocker stops, NoCapOS switches it back.
sh.p53.title: Port 53
sh.p53.hint: The system's own resolver is sitting on port 53 for this machine. Free it so the blocker can answer everywhere.
sh.p53.freedHint: NoCapOS freed port 53 from the system resolver. You can give it back anytime.
sh.p53.lanNote: For now the blocker answers on this machine's own addresses only, which works fine for your network.
sh.p53.freeMsg: The system resolver stops listening on port 53 and this machine keeps looking names up the same way as before.
sh.setup.title: Point your devices here
sh.setup.hint: Blocking only works for devices that ask this server.
sh.setup.router: Best move: open your router's settings and set its DNS server (often under DHCP or LAN).
sh.setup.devices: Or set it on one device at a time in its Wi-Fi or network settings.
sh.setup.check: Reconnect, then watch Receipts: your device should show up.
sh.lists.title: Block lists
sh.allow.title: Never block
sh.allow.hint: Something broke? Put its domain here. Wins over every list.
sh.block.title: Always block
sh.block.hint: Your own blocks, one domain per line. Subdomains included.
sh.rec.title: Local names
sh.rec.hint: Give devices on your network easy names, like nas.home.
sh.logs.privacy: Kept on this server only. Turn it off or shorten it in Settings.
sh.logs.off: The query log is off, so there's nothing to show. Privacy mode fr.
sh.logs.clearMsg: Every saved lookup is deleted for good.
sh.logs.devicesHint: Who asked what in the last day. Tap one to see its lookups.
sh.logs.blockedHint: What the firewall turned away in the last day. Logging has to be on.
sh.logs.noBlocked: Nothing got bounced. Or logging's off.
sh.set.upstreamsHint: Where allowed lookups go. Tried in order, one per line.
sh.set.cnamesHint: Also block answers that point at a blocked name.
sh.set.privacyHint: The log never leaves this server.
sh.set.logHint: Needed for top lists and the per-device view.
sh.set.logClientsHint: Off: the log keeps domains, not who.
sh.set.ipv6Hint: Same rules for IPv6. Keep this on unless you know why not.
